Bilabial stop 'with accompanying velar constriction but with lip rounding only when preceded or followed by a back, rounded vowel' (p. xvi). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).
'A voiceless, dental or alveolar stop, unaspirated' (p. xvi). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).

Bilabial nasal 'without accompanying velar constriction or lip rounding', tending (unless double) to be denasalised between vowels, 'where it approaches a bilabial flap' (p. xv). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).

Bilabial nasal 'with accompanying velar constriction but with lip rounding only when preceded or followed by a back, rounded vowel', tending (unless double) to be denasalised between vowels (pp. xv-xvi). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).

'A voiced, dental or alveolar, nasal continuant' (p. xvi). Lagoon n continues both n and l, which stay distinct in the Hall Islands, Mortlockese and Puluwatese (pp. xi, xv). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).
Velar nasal, tending (unless double) 'to be partially denasalized between vowels, where it approaches a velar flap' (p. xvi). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).
'An alveolar trill' (p. xvi). Long (double) consonants are written twice (p. xiv).
'A bilabial glide, unrounded except when preceded or followed by a back rounded vowel' (p. xvii).
'An alveo-palatal glide, unrounded', not written word-initially, 'where it is phonetically absent in some dialects' (p. xvii).
